sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Celina, Texas, and which route is fastest?
sections.html:
The fastest way to sell a Celina house is usually a direct sale to a cash buyer, because there is no listing period, no buyer loan to approve and no repair list to complete first. The slower routes, a listing with an agent or a sale by owner, can bring a higher price when the house is in good condition and you have time.

  • Choose an agent listing if the house shows well and you can wait for a buyer's lender to finish.
  • Choose a sale by owner if you are comfortable writing the contract and screening buyers.
  • Choose a cash sale if the house needs work, is tenant occupied, is in an estate or has a looming sale date.

sections.h2: Where is Celina, and how did the town begin?
sections.html:
Celina sits on State Highway 289 and Farm Road 455, about fifteen miles northwest of McKinney and twelve miles north of Frisco in northwestern Collin County, according to the Texas State Historical Association. The Handbook of Texas says it was established in 1879 and named by a settler for his native Celina, Tennessee, and that a post office opened in 1881.

The town moved in 1902, when a railway reached the area, to a site one mile north of the first one. It incorporated in 1907, and by 1915 it had the first road in Collin County built just for automobiles, Celina Pike. Population fell during the Depression, from 1,126 in 1920 to 994 in 1940, and then rose after the war to 1,861 by 2000. The city's own site now describes rapid growth that it wants to balance with the town's heritage.

That scale of change is the reason a Celina seller should check the date on any document: a survey, a plat or a permit from a decade ago may describe a very different lot, street or utility layout.

sections.h2: What does Celina's permit office require when I fix up or finish work?
sections.html:
Celina's Building Services Division requires a permit to erect, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert, move or demolish any structure inside the city limits. Residential permits go through the city's residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 or permits@celina-tx.gov, at 112 N. Colorado St.

The division states these working rules:

  • Office hours are Monday through Thursday, 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM.
  • Inspectors work Monday through Thursday, 6:30 AM to 4:30 PM, with a 3:30 PM daily cut-off for requests.
  • A permit expires on the 181st day if no inspection has occurred or no progress has been shown, and an application is abandoned if no permit is issued within 180 days.
  • Starting in February 2026, applications and inspections follow the 2024 International Code Council codes plus the 2023 National Electrical Code with amendments.
  • Residential permits submitted after December 8, 2025 use the MGO Connect portal; older ones stay in MyGov.

If you pulled a permit for a pool, a garage conversion or a roof and never closed it, call the permit desk before you list. An unfinished permit can delay a title company even when the work looks complete.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district sets the value of my Celina house?
sections.html:
Collin County houses are valued by the Collin Central Appraisal District, and its homepage says the 2026 appraisal notices for real property were mailed on April 15. The district also has a page on a homestead exemption audit tied to Senate Bill 1801 and links to a tax transparency site where an owner can see the taxing units on a bill.

Read the appraisal district name on your own statement, since a Celina address near a county line may be on a different roll. Then go to that district's site and check three things: the exemptions on the account, the value history and the taxing units listed.

The state rules that sit behind every Texas bill are short. The Comptroller says taxes are due upon receipt in October and are delinquent after January 31, and that a lien attaches to the property as of January 1. Penalties start at six percent plus one percent interest the first month. Unpaid taxes show up in the buyer's title review, so ask your title company how the year's bill will be handled.

sections.h2: What does Texas give Celina homeowners as a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
A Celina owner who lives in the house as a main residence can claim the Texas residence homestead exemption, which in school districts is $140,000, according to the Comptroller. Anyone 65 or older or disabled gets an extra $60,000 from the school district and a ceiling on school taxes. Disabled veterans can qualify for partial or full exemptions, and the page prints the bracket amounts from $5,000 up to $12,000 by disability rating.

The Comptroller also states that the home's appraised value for tax purposes may not rise more than 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place, starting in the year after it is first qualified. A buyer who plans to live in the house can apply after closing. If you inherited a Celina house and are not on a recorded deed, the appraisal district asks for an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: How are Celina deeds recorded and what does it cost?
sections.html:
A deed for a Celina house is recorded in the real property records of the county clerk where the land lies. It must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer. Under the state's clerk manual, the first page costs $5.00 and each added page $4.00, and the clerk may charge a records management fee up to $10, an archive fee up to $10 and a technology fee of $2.00.

The manual also says a missing grantee mailing address can add a fee. Put the buyer's mailing address on the deed and ask the title company to confirm the legal description matches the plat for your section of town.

sections.h2: What if my Celina house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Texas sets deadlines for each of these, and the Texas State Law Library explains them in plain terms.

  • Inheritance: a will can be probated for four years after death. Heirs without a will may use a small estate affidavit only if the assets, excluding homestead and exempt property, total $75,000 or less. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the county clerk, and no law forces a third party to accept it.
  • Tenants: unless the lease says otherwise, a landlord gives at least 3 days of written notice to vacate. A justice court suit follows, with the hearing set between 10 and 21 days after filing, and a writ of possession can come 6 days after judgment.
  • Foreclosure: the lender sends a notice of default, and a borrower has 20 days from receipt to reinstate by paying the past-due amount. Sales are held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of a month.

If any of these apply, talk to a Texas attorney or the county clerk before signing a sale contract, and tell the buyer about the situation at the start.

sections.h2: What should a Celina seller collect before asking for offers?
sections.html:
A short folder saves days at closing. Gather the items below before you ask for offers.

  • The most recent tax statement and the appraisal district account number.
  • Any open permit number, and the final inspection record for finished work.
  • The mortgage payoff figure, if there is a loan.
  • Any HOA contact and dues balance.
  • Lease copies, if a tenant lives in the house.

faqs.q: How long does a Celina building permit stay valid?
faqs.a: A Celina permit expires on the 181st day if no inspection has taken place or no progress has been shown. An application with no permit issued within 180 days is treated as abandoned. Call the residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 for an exact status.

faqs.q: Do Celina homeowners pay a city tax separate from the county?
faqs.a: Texas has no state property tax, and the local units that tax your address each set their own rate. Your tax statement lists every unit. Ask the tax office for the current adopted rates before you do any math.

faqs.q: Is Celina in Collin County or Denton County?
faqs.a: The Handbook of Texas places Celina in northwestern Collin County, and the Collin Central Appraisal District values Collin County property. Read the district named on your own tax statement to confirm which roll your house is on.

faqs.q: What does a probate shortcut cost a Celina heir?
faqs.a: The state describes a small estate affidavit and a muniment of title as informal methods, and both need court approval. Fees and requirements vary by court, so ask the county clerk for the current filing schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Celina house before I finish the repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is. The main issue is an open permit, which you should disclose and, if possible, resolve with the city's permit desk first.
